## 05:15 UTC — Concrete integer multiplication speed-up behind `subnlogn` (Claude, branch claude/loving-hopper-sdpt73, PR #4958)


- Rewrote `isogeny_algos/src/subnlogn/fastint.rs` (Fermat-ring Schönhage–Strassen): fixed-width limb buffers with in-place butterflies, shifts, folds and carry pass instead of fresh `Big` values per operation; one forward transform when squaring; transform length chosen by a small cost model; cutoffs `BASE_BITS = 2^17` product bits, `LEAF_BITS = 2^14`.
- `Big::mul` in `isogeny_algos/src/bigint.rs` now uses Karatsuba above 32 limbs; the quadratic loop is kept as `Big::mul_schoolbook` for test oracles.
- New tests: Karatsuba vs schoolbook on all shape pairs; ring primitives vs `Big` modular oracles; transform round trip including the 2^K endpoint; forced deep recursion; plan validity. `tests/subnlogn.rs`: the published base-case receipt test now asserts the Fermat branch ran exactly when the product exceeds `BASE_BITS`, and adds a 2100×2060-limb case that runs it.
- Added `examples/fastint_timing.rs` (development wall-clock diagnostic, every product checked for equality).
- Checks (Rust 1.97.0, local): default lib 55 passed / 1 pre-existing ignored; feature lib 122 passed / 1 ignored; `tests/subnlogn` 10 passed; example harnesses passed; ntt/polyfast/powmod 10 passed; clippy `-D warnings` exit 0; rustfmt on touched files exit 0; `subnlogn -- --full` and `subnlogn_full_flow` exit 0 with known answers matched.
- Local interleaved timing, origin/main f0ca664e vs branch, best of 3 rounds, 4-vCPU cloud VM, no PMU, not isolated (unverified development observation, not a benchmark record): fastint 4 Mbit-operand product 0.874 s → 0.052 s; 1 Mbit 0.115 s → 0.012 s; 262 kbit 0.0264 s → 0.0015 s; best available multiplier 1.5–2.6× faster at 2–32 kbit (Karatsuba), 9–17× at ≥ 262 kbit.


- Did not try to accelerate via the sub-n log n construction itself: its saving factor (lg n)^(2^-182) is ≈ 1 at every physical size, so the practical lever is the classical prerequisite that actually runs.
- Kept results exact and every leaf on the crate's own arithmetic (no external crates, no floating point).
- Timings stay local development diagnostics; no `benchmarks/` row or bench.record was produced, since the result is not an IC/ECDLP measurement and was not run on isolab.


- Optional: a formal isolab-eks benchmark (bench.record/v1) if the speed-up is to be cited as a result.
- Further levers not done: dedicated Karatsuba squaring, √2 trick / truncated transforms to remove the power-of-two-length rounding, a tuned multithreaded pointwise stage.
- `examples/subnlogn -- --full` now reports `prerequisite_transform_nodes: 0` for its small input (below the new cutoff); the historical construction-correctness receipts pin their own commit and are unchanged.


- First deep-recursion test computed the ring size for a·b and reused it for a·a (test bug, fixed). After the cost-model planner landed, one case recursed only one level; the test now requires depth ≥ 2 in at least one case and checks every product.
- `git worktree` failed inside the absorbed submodule gitdir; used `git archive origin/main` into the scratchpad for the baseline build instead.

## 16:40 UTC — Follow-up: squaring, ring sizing, threads (Claude, PR #4958)


- `bigint.rs`: `sqr_limbs` (schoolbook squaring below 48 limbs, Karatsuba squaring above); `mul_limbs`/`Big::mul` route equal operands to it.
- `fastint.rs`: nodes with K >= 2^19 split the low transform stages and the pointwise products over `std::thread::scope` workers and run the two forward transforms concurrently; `fastint::set_threads(n)` caps workers (1 disables; products are identical for every setting); plans are memoized.
- Tried and reverted: choosing the top-level ring size jointly with the dimensions, and a recursive granule search, to remove child-ring overshoot at power-of-two product lengths.
- Local interleaved timing (best of 3, 4-vCPU cloud VM, no PMU, unverified development observation): squaring 1.5–1.7× faster below the 2^17-bit cutoff and 1.1–1.3× above; threads (auto vs 1) 1.25–1.55× at 262–441 kbit operands, 1.6–1.9× at 0.5–0.9 Mbit, 1.8–2.6× at ≥1 Mbit; no change below the threshold. Versus origin/main the 4.19 Mbit operand product goes 1.11 s → 0.022 s.


- Reverted the joint ring sizing: v1 and v2 single-thread timings agreed within noise (ratio ≈1.00 across 13 kbit–4.2 Mbit), so it added complexity without a measured gain. The ≈2× step from 2.97 to 4.19 Mbit persisted with it, so that step is not ring rounding (likely cache size; not investigated).
- Raised the threading threshold from K >= 2^18 to 2^19 after measuring 0.76–0.88× (slower) at 131–185 kbit operands with the lower threshold.
- Threads default to all cores; `set_threads(1)` exists for isolated single-core measurement elsewhere in the lab.


- The 2.97 → 4.19 Mbit step (likely cache); a cache-oblivious or blocked transform order would be the next lever.
- PR CI: red jobs (backend-leaderboard frozen report, lab-parity, gates, artifact-cache scope) are also red on main 7d61e3b4 and do not touch `isogeny_algos`.


- An edit script dropped the `GRANULE_STEPS` constant (compile error, restored). The threaded-products test first required more than one transform node; the children were Karatsuba leaves, so it now requires more than zero.

## 2026-11-23 04:28 UTC — Target quotient structure and exact native controls (PR #4952)


- Completed the written fixed-subset quotient argument: for fixed W in the split selector, the canonical remainder has generic rank min(d,2|W|). - The immutable-source Rust qualifier built and ran on its first attempt within the frozen 60 s / 2 GiB envelope: 91 finite target records (including category duplicates), 52 cusp minors,20 empty controls, 35,391 quotient-grid/reconstructed-coefficient comparisons and 4,171 F97 exhaustive root checks. Separate-role same-host replay reproduced the full 168,796-byte stdout, with stable source/binary hashes. Producer and replay receipts are retained under target_quotient/evidence/. [pcc:unverified]
- On the fixed Prime31 d=63 fixture, X=0/2 give e=68, coefficient rank 63, zero support 0 and Boolean rank 0; selector target X=1 gives e=67, rank 62, 133 zero cells and Boolean rank 34. These are algebraic finite-fixture observations, not signed relation counts, random-target yield or performance. [pcc:unverified]
- Issued fixed d=6/k=2 evaluated identity IDC1h7e169f28f6a50bb6 (degree 12, proof:null); producer checks 32 issuer + 32 extra points and expression/digest tamper controls. Separate-role check used 32 fresh seeded points. Source and certificate custody remain unchanged. [pcc:unverified]

Ledger prefix/chain check returned zero at 1,556 entries; historical rejected missing-type claims remained unchanged. [pcc:unverified]
- Wrote the source-linked REPORT.md and PROOF_MAP.md; report prose lint has zero findings. The presentation-only renderer is preparing the illustrated PDF from retained native values. Native dependencies and all frozen predecessor artifacts remain unchanged. [pcc:unverified]

### Decisions and interpretation

- The actual radical quotient is distinguished from the nonreduced polynomial used as a minor witness; the cusp radical is t. Generic coefficient rank is not a rank formula for a collided finite-field quotient or a rootfinding lower bound.
- Coefficient/evaluation rank and Boolean zero-support rank are different observables. Existing Fermat-projector and nonunit formulations are attributed to prior notes. The next algorithmic obligation is an exact empty-query and root-extraction method that charges setup, quotient operations and witness/sign recovery. No competing signed extractor was implemented.

- Lean/Lake remain unavailable; no formal proof or signed execution verdict is asserted. No admitted benchmark or paid compute ran. The fixed degree set stops at 63 and does not establish d=1302 behavior.

Both setup failures are retained; they are not upstream-source defects. The root gate remains unqualified and the frozen retry envelope was not expanded. [pcc:unverified]

## 2026-11-23T07:30:00Z — Large-prime graph follow-ups to #4929

### What was done (commands, files, features)

- `src/cryptanalysis/large_prime_graph/block_wiedemann.rs` (catalog item 6):
  block Krylov sequence, σ-basis matrix generator with shifted degrees,
  λ-stripped Horner reconstruction, verified kernel vectors; bordered
  `A x = b` with a preconditioned (`A P`, `P = I + R`) retry. `tests/block_wiedemann.rs` (5 tests).
- `ecbench_large_prime::SolveOptions::capture_relations` (opt-in, default off,
  never serialized) and `examples/lp_graph_collect.rs`: real relation streams
  through `large_prime_graph::eval`; `examples/block_wiedemann_eval.rs`.
- Fixed `crypto::` → `crypto_lib::` in the #4929 tests/examples.
- In the real crate on `main` 7d61e3b45 (`src/bin/hecx.rs` stubbed locally,
  not committed): `cargo test --release --test large_prime_graph --test
  block_wiedemann` → 13/13 and 5/5.
- Runs and write-up: `research/lp_graph_algorithms_20261123/` (README sections
  "Real relation streams", "Block Wiedemann schedule"; `results_real/`,
  `block_wiedemann/`, `figure_followup.svg`, `report_followup.pdf`).
- Lean: crypto-lean#32 merged with `CryptoLean/Combinatorics/GainDsu.lean`
  (catalog §6 rank formula; proof gate PASS 338 thm, 0 trusted).
- Sources checked: KB unavailable (no research-kb MCP in this session).

### Decisions made (and why)

- Capture via an opt-in option rather than a new collector, so the evaluated
  batch is byte-for-byte what `filter_large_primes` receives.
- Bordered solve retries with a random sparse right preconditioner: without
  it, matrices with `ker A ∩ range A ≠ 0` only yield kernel vectors in the
  range (last coordinate 0).

### Open threads (unfinished, pick up next time)

- `src/bin/hecx.rs` on `main` has unclosed delimiters (lines 160, 327, 597, 766);
  integration tests cannot build until it is repaired.
- Prime-field and Gaudry-cubic collectors do not expose their streams yet.
- Overlap: ACTIVE item `claude/intelligent-babbage-u5acwr` (`ic_graph/`) covers
  the same catalog; reuse `large_prime_graph` rather than duplicating.

### Errors (what went wrong, how it was handled)

- The #4929 tests used the wrong crate name (`crypto`); hidden because CI could
  not build `main` and the standalone check crate was named `crypto`. Fixed here.
- `--graph orbit` needs a Koblitz instance; added `--koblitz`.

## 05:15 UTC — Concrete integer multiplication speed-up behind `subnlogn` (Claude, branch claude/loving-hopper-sdpt73, PR #4958)


- Rewrote `isogeny_algos/src/subnlogn/fastint.rs` (Fermat-ring Schönhage–Strassen): fixed-width limb buffers with in-place butterflies, shifts, folds and carry pass instead of fresh `Big` values per operation; one forward transform when squaring; transform length chosen by a small cost model; cutoffs `BASE_BITS = 2^17` product bits, `LEAF_BITS = 2^14`.
- `Big::mul` in `isogeny_algos/src/bigint.rs` now uses Karatsuba above 32 limbs; the quadratic loop is kept as `Big::mul_schoolbook` for test oracles.
- New tests: Karatsuba vs schoolbook on all shape pairs; ring primitives vs `Big` modular oracles; transform round trip including the 2^K endpoint; forced deep recursion; plan validity. `tests/subnlogn.rs`: the published base-case receipt test now asserts the Fermat branch ran exactly when the product exceeds `BASE_BITS`, and adds a 2100×2060-limb case that runs it.
- Added `examples/fastint_timing.rs` (development wall-clock diagnostic, every product checked for equality).
- Checks (Rust 1.97.0, local): default lib 55 passed / 1 pre-existing ignored; feature lib 122 passed / 1 ignored; `tests/subnlogn` 10 passed; example harnesses passed; ntt/polyfast/powmod 10 passed; clippy `-D warnings` exit 0; rustfmt on touched files exit 0; `subnlogn -- --full` and `subnlogn_full_flow` exit 0 with known answers matched.
- Local interleaved timing, origin/main f0ca664e vs branch, best of 3 rounds, 4-vCPU cloud VM, no PMU, not isolated (unverified development observation, not a benchmark record): fastint 4 Mbit-operand product 0.874 s → 0.052 s; 1 Mbit 0.115 s → 0.012 s; 262 kbit 0.0264 s → 0.0015 s; best available multiplier 1.5–2.6× faster at 2–32 kbit (Karatsuba), 9–17× at ≥ 262 kbit.


- Did not try to accelerate via the sub-n log n construction itself: its saving factor (lg n)^(2^-182) is ≈ 1 at every physical size, so the practical lever is the classical prerequisite that actually runs.
- Kept results exact and every leaf on the crate's own arithmetic (no external crates, no floating point).
- Timings stay local development diagnostics; no `benchmarks/` row or bench.record was produced, since the result is not an IC/ECDLP measurement and was not run on isolab.


- Optional: a formal isolab-eks benchmark (bench.record/v1) if the speed-up is to be cited as a result.
- Further levers not done: dedicated Karatsuba squaring, √2 trick / truncated transforms to remove the power-of-two-length rounding, a tuned multithreaded pointwise stage.
- `examples/subnlogn -- --full` now reports `prerequisite_transform_nodes: 0` for its small input (below the new cutoff); the historical construction-correctness receipts pin their own commit and are unchanged.


- First deep-recursion test computed the ring size for a·b and reused it for a·a (test bug, fixed). After the cost-model planner landed, one case recursed only one level; the test now requires depth ≥ 2 in at least one case and checks every product.

## 16:40 UTC — Follow-up: squaring, ring sizing, threads (Claude, PR #4958)


- `bigint.rs`: `sqr_limbs` (schoolbook squaring below 48 limbs, Karatsuba squaring above); `mul_limbs`/`Big::mul` route equal operands to it.
- `fastint.rs`: nodes with K >= 2^19 split the low transform stages and the pointwise products over `std::thread::scope` workers and run the two forward transforms concurrently; `fastint::set_threads(n)` caps workers (1 disables; products are identical for every setting); plans are memoized.
- Tried and reverted: choosing the top-level ring size jointly with the dimensions, and a recursive granule search, to remove child-ring overshoot at power-of-two product lengths.
